The Laredo City Council has approved a new ordinance tightening oversight of fiber-optic work in the city, according to the Laredo Morning Times.

Under the measure, fiber-optic companies must register with the city, obtain permits, maintain insurance and follow construction and safety rules, the Times reported.

The ordinance — Ordinance No. 2026-O-195 — amends Chapter 28, Article IX of the city's Code of Ordinances, which governs utility coordination and work in public rights of way. Among its provisions, it limits each fiber-optic company to no more than three active subdivision installation projects at a time, and subjects right-of-way permits to review through the city's Utility Coordination Committee, according to the ordinance text published by the city.

The ordinance states the rules are meant to protect public health, safety and welfare and to be competitively neutral, without imposing fees for use of the public right of way or materially inhibiting broadband service.

Sources: Laredo Morning Times; City of Laredo, Ordinance No. 2026-O-195.
